sources: Jonah 1:1-3 (God tells Jonah to go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; Jonah flees to Tarshish from Joppa)
Jonah 1:4-5 (a mighty storm; the sailors were afraid)
Jonah 1:12 (“Take me up, and throw me into the sea. Then the sea will be calm for you”)
Jonah 1:15-17 (they threw him in; the sea ceased raging; God prepared a great fish; three days and three nights)
Jonah 2:1 (Jonah prayed from the fish’s belly); Jonah 2:10 (the fish vomited Jonah out on the dry land)
Jonah 3:1 (“The word of the Lord came to Jonah the second time”)
Jonah 3:3-10 (he went; the people believed God, fasted, put on sackcloth, the king too; God relented)
Jonah 4:1-2 (Jonah was angry: “I knew that you are a gracious God and merciful”); 4:6 (the plant); 4:10-11 (“Shouldn’t I be concerned for Nineveh, that great city?”)
Hebrew dag gadol, “a great fish,” not specifically a whale
Matthew 12:39-41 (the sign of Jonah: three days and three nights; Nineveh repented), behind the teach step
check: Jonah (Yunus) is a prophet in Islam; all paintings show him only from behind or far away. The king of Nineveh is shown small in a crowd.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? ever run from something you knew you were supposed to do?
options: then you’re in good company. listen to this one.
then you know how jonah felt. listen.
good. keep this one for the day you want to run.

steps.line: God told Jonah to go to the great city of Nineveh and warn it. Jonah didn’t want to. He got on a ship sailing the opposite way.
steps.label: Jonah 1:1-3

steps.line: A great storm hit the sea. The sailors were terrified. Jonah told them, “Throw me into the sea, and it will grow calm.”
steps.label: Jonah 1:4-12

steps.q: Jonah tells the sailors to throw him overboard. What do they do first?
o: Throw him in at once to save themselves
Row hard for land, trying to save him
Draw lots again to be sure
steps.why: They row hard for shore, the book says, but the storm only grows. Only then, praying, do they throw him in, and the sea goes calm.

steps.line: The sea grew calm. God sent a great fish to swallow Jonah. He was inside it three days and three nights, and there he prayed.
steps.label: Jonah 1:15-2:1

steps.line: Then the fish spat Jonah out onto dry land.
steps.label: Jonah 2:10

steps.line: Then comes a line readers treasure: “The word of the Lord came to Jonah a second time.”
steps.label: Jonah 3:1

steps.q: Jonah heard God the first time, and ran. Why do readers love the words “a second time” so much?
o: God didn’t give up on him or replace him
Jonah hadn’t heard the message clearly
It warned him there would be no third chance
steps.why: He had heard, and run. God came back to the same runaway anyway. That’s mercy.

steps.line: This time Jonah went. The whole city listened, from the king down. They turned from their wrong ways, and God spared them.
steps.label: Jonah 3:3-10

steps.q: Nineveh was the capital of Assyria. Why would a prophet of Israel not want to save it?
o: Nineveh was too far to walk to
steps.why: Assyria’s armies were the terror of the region, and would later conquer Israel’s northern kingdom. Saving Nineveh felt like saving your worst enemy.

steps.q: The whole city turns, and God spares it. How does Jonah feel?
o: So angry he asks to die
Relieved, and ready to go home
steps.why: He’s furious, and tells God why he ran in the first place: he knew God was gracious and merciful, and would forgive them.

steps.line: But Jonah was angry. “I knew you are a gracious and merciful God,” he said. God asked him, “Shouldn’t I care about that great city?”
steps.label: Jonah 4:1-11

say: here’s what i love. God didn’t find a better prophet. he spoke to the same runaway again.

jesus himself pointed to jonah’s three days in the fish as a sign of his own three days in the tomb. and christians read the whole book as mercy: for the one who ran, and for the city he didn’t want saved.

steps.q: God gave Jonah a second chance. Then Jonah was angry when God gave Nineveh one too. What is the book asking you?
o: Was Nineveh truly sorry, or just scared?
Should a prophet obey God the first time?
Can you be glad when your enemy gets mercy too?
steps.why: The book ends on God’s question, with no answer from Jonah. It leaves the answer to the reader.

today.say: God gave jonah a second chance, and nineveh one too. today, give someone a second chance, especially someone you’d rather not: answer the message, say good morning, let one old thing go.
options: then say it today. a second time is how God works in this story.
it is. even jonah struggled with it. start with something small.
